newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain needs no special deal for EMU entry - Matutes.
newsitem.headline: Spain needs no special deal for EMU entry - Matutes.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Thursday that his country needed no special concessions to win a place in the first wave to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
"Spain will meet the targets...Spain doesn't need, nor want, any shady deal to meet the Maastricht criteria," Matutes told a news conference.
Matutes added Spain would not tolerate doubts from abroad that it may not make the first wave.
Although the Maastricht criteria on public debt dictates this should be below 60 percent of GDP, Matutes said it would be calculated taking into consideration the trend.
"There are many countries which are thought likely to be part of EMU from the start which have higher debt than Spain," he added.
On Wednesday, Spain's Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said Spanish debt had reached 69.3 percent of GDP at the end of 1996, four points higher than in 1995.
